```{r setup, include=FALSE, cache=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = FALSE, warning=FALSE, message=FALSE)

v2_dir <- "results_v2_cache"
dir.create(v2_dir, showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)
dir.create(file.path(v2_dir, "models"), showWarnings = FALSE)
dir.create(file.path(v2_dir, "derived"), showWarnings = FALSE)
v2_inputs <- c("all_withNorway_noTest_countryFill_raw.csv", "GCI.csv",
               "IH_measurement_invariance.rds", "AOT_measurement_invariance.rds",
               "IC_measurement_invariance.rds", "mH1_exploi.RDS", "m_all_exploi.RDS")
v2_packages <- c("knitr", "lme4", "mgcv", "gamm4", "lavaan", "dplyr",
                 "tidyr", "ggplot2", "gt", "broom", "psych", "kableExtra")
v2_signature <- digest::digest(list(
  tools::md5sum(v2_inputs), R.version.string,
  setNames(lapply(v2_packages, function(p) as.character(packageVersion(p))), v2_packages)
))
knitr::opts_chunk$set(cache = TRUE, cache.lazy = FALSE,
  cache.path = file.path(v2_dir, paste0("knitr-", knitr::opts_knit$get("rmarkdown.pandoc.to"), "/")),
  fig.path = "results_v2_files/figure-", error = FALSE)
set.seed(20261016)

# Hash the CURRENT upstream R code on every render, not the prose or captions.
# This propagates changes to data preparation and helper functions downstream.
v2_lines <- readLines(knitr::current_input(dir = TRUE), warn = FALSE)
v2_starts <- grep("^```\\{r", v2_lines)
v2_code_keys <- character(length(v2_starts))
v2_labels <- character(length(v2_starts))
v2_unnamed <- 0L
v2_previous <- "results-v2-code-v1"
for (i in seq_along(v2_starts)) {
  start <- v2_starts[i]
  end <- start + which(v2_lines[(start + 1L):length(v2_lines)] == "```")[1]
  code <- v2_lines[(start + 1L):(end - 1L)]
  header <- sub("^```\\{r", "", v2_lines[start])
  header <- sub("\\}$", "", header)
  label <- trimws(strsplit(header, ",", fixed = TRUE)[[1]][1])
  yaml_label <- grep("^#\\| label:", code, value = TRUE)
  if (length(yaml_label)) label <- trimws(sub("^#\\| label:", "", yaml_label[1]))
  if (is.na(label) || !nzchar(label)) {
    v2_unnamed <- v2_unnamed + 1L
    label <- paste0("unnamed-chunk-", v2_unnamed)
  }
  v2_labels[i] <- label
  code <- code[!grepl("^\\s*#\\|", code)]
  v2_previous <- digest::digest(list(v2_previous, parse(text = code, keep.source = FALSE)))
  v2_code_keys[i] <- v2_previous
}
names(v2_code_keys) <- v2_labels
knitr::opts_hooks$set(cache = function(options) {
  if (isTRUE(options$cache)) {
    key <- v2_code_keys[options$label]
    if (length(key) != 1L || is.na(key)) stop("No cache dependency key for ", options$label)
    options$cache.extra <- list(v2_signature, unname(key))
  }
  options
})


v2_fit <- function(expr) {
  call <- substitute(expr)
  env <- parent.frame()
  data <- eval(call$data, envir = env)
  key <- digest::digest(list(call = paste(deparse(call), collapse = "\n"),
                            data = data, signature = v2_signature))
  path <- file.path(v2_dir, "models", paste0(as.character(call[[1]]), "-", key, ".rds"))
  if (file.exists(path)) return(readRDS(path))
  fit <- eval(call, envir = env)
  tmp <- tempfile(tmpdir = dirname(path))
  saveRDS(fit, tmp)
  if (!file.rename(tmp, path)) stop("Could not save model cache: ", path)
  fit
}

library(lme4)

  theme_bw(
    base_size = base_size,
    base_family = base_family
  ) +
    theme(
      text = element_text(
        family = base_family,
        size = base_size
      ),

      panel.border = element_blank(),

      strip.background = element_rect(
        fill = "white",
        colour = NA
      ),
      strip.text = element_text(
        size = rel(0.8)
      ),

      panel.grid.major.x = element_blank(),
      panel.grid.major.y = element_blank(),
      panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),

      axis.line = element_line(
        linewidth = 0.4
      ),
      axis.text.x = element_text(
        size = 7,
        colour = "black"
      ),
      axis.text.y = element_text(
        size = 7,
        colour = "black"
      ),
      axis.ticks = element_line(
        colour = "black"
      )
    )
}

# Reading and rebuilding this report {.unnumbered}

This report retains the analyses and model specifications in `results.qmd`, separates confirmatory tests from robustness checks and exploratory analyses, and completes the trial-level confidence-resolution and continuous-collectivism analyses. The local preregistration is [PSA-JTF3 EC Manuscript.pdf](<PSA-JTF3 EC Manuscript.pdf>).

Render with `quarto render results_v2.qmd --to html` (or `--to docx` / `--to pdf`). The first render fits uncached models. Subsequent renders reuse intermediate objects and output in `results_v2_cache/knitr-*` and fitted models in `results_v2_cache/models`. Input-file checksums, R/package versions, and upstream analysis code invalidate chunk caches; model caches additionally track the fitting call and its actual data. Editing narrative text does not refit models. To force recomputation of all active analyses, remove only `results_v2_cache` before rendering. Existing source files and saved models are read only.

The existing measurement-invariance objects and the original individual-difference models are retained as **legacy fitted results**: their provenance cannot be verified from the saved objects alone. The original, disabled refitting code is retained for reference; those results are not silently presented as newly fitted models. Written interpretations inherited from the original report should be checked against the tables after any data or model change.

**Analysis notes.** The original code includes CAPTCHA scores equal to 0.5 (`>= 0.5`), whereas the preregistration excludes them. That cutoff is retained here for comparability. The exclusion-table total is corrected to include the residence exclusion. The confidence-resolution models retain the working specification with fixed problem effects and participant random intercepts; the preregistration instead specifies random intercepts for both participant and problem. The revised individual-difference models retain the original omission of AOT. The calibration models retain the original treatment of missing/excluded trials when summing accuracy.

# Results

## Data Processing and Exclusions


Exclusion criteria applied as stated in the [preregistration](https://osf.io/preprints/psyarxiv/wegc5_v1):

> We will exclude participants who did not complete the study, failed an attention check question, failed to pass the Captcha test (i.e., their Captcha score is equal to or lower than 0.5), or are not permanent residents of the geopolitical region where data collection is taking place.

```{r v2-chunk-003, echo=FALSE}
total_initial <- nrow(d)

excluded_finished <- total_initial  - nrow(d %>% filter(Finished == 1))
remaining_after_finished <- nrow(d %>% filter(Finished == 1))

excluded_recaptcha <- remaining_after_finished - nrow(d %>% filter(Finished == 1, 
                                                                   Q_RecaptchaScore >= 0.5))
remaining_after_recaptcha <- nrow(d %>% filter(Finished == 1, 
                                               Q_RecaptchaScore >= 0.5))

excluded_attcheck <- remaining_after_recaptcha - nrow(d %>% filter(Finished == 1, 
                                                                   Q_RecaptchaScore >= 0.5,
                                                                   check==0))
remaining_after_attcheck <- nrow(d %>% filter(Finished == 1, 
                                               Q_RecaptchaScore >= 0.5,
                                               check==0))

excluded_residence <- remaining_after_attcheck - nrow(d %>% filter(Finished == 1, 
                                                                   Q_RecaptchaScore >= 0.5,
                                                                   check==0,
                                                                   Country_Res_YN =="Yes"))
remaining_after_residence <- nrow(d %>% filter(Finished == 1, 
                                               Q_RecaptchaScore >= 0.5,
                                               check==0,
                                               Country_Res_YN =="Yes"))

total_excluded <- total_initial - remaining_after_residence

summary_table <- data.frame(
  Criterion = c( "Finished == 1", 
                 "Q_RecaptchaScore >= 0.5", 
                 "attention check == 0",
                 "Country_Res_YN == Yes",
                 "Total"),
  Excluded = c(excluded_finished, 
               excluded_recaptcha, 
               excluded_attcheck,
               excluded_residence,
               total_excluded),
  Fraction = c(excluded_finished/total_initial, 
               excluded_recaptcha/total_initial, 
               excluded_attcheck/total_initial,
               excluded_residence/total_initial, 
               total_excluded/total_initial),
  Percentage = c(excluded_finished/total_initial * 100, 
                 excluded_recaptcha/total_initial * 100, 
                 excluded_attcheck/total_initial * 100,
                 excluded_residence/total_initial * 100, 
                 total_excluded/total_initial * 100)
)

kable(summary_table, booktabs = TRUE, 
      col.names = c("Exclusion Criterion", 
                    "Number Excluded", 
                    "Fraction Excluded", 
                    "Percentage Excluded"), 
      caption="Each line indicates how many participants failed each criterion (applied sequentially).")
```

library(dplyr)

education_table <- d %>%
  filter(!is.na(Edu), !is.na(culture)) %>%
  mutate(
    Edu = factor(
      Edu,
      levels = c(
        "Less than a high school or secondary school degree (or equivalent)",

        "Bachelor’s degree (or equivalent)",
        "Postgraduate degree (MA, PhD, JD, etc.)",

    `N (%)` = sprintf("%s (%.1f%%)", format(N, big.mark = ","), percent)

  ungroup() %>%
  select(Education = Edu, culture, `N (%)`) %>%
  pivot_wider(
    names_from = culture,
    values_from = `N (%)`
  )

    col.names = c(

      "Collectivistic, N (%)",

### Use of external resources


```{r v2-chunk-009, echo=FALSE}
d %>%
  mutate(
    participant = row_number(),
    condition = case_when(
      feedback == "F"  & justification == "NJ" ~ "Feedback",
      feedback == "NF" & justification == "J"  ~ "Justification",
      feedback == "F"  & justification == "J"  ~ "Feedback + justification",
      .default = "Baseline"
    ),
    condition = factor(
      condition,
      levels = c(
        "Baseline",
        "Feedback",
        "Justification",
        "Feedback + justification"
      )
    )
  ) %>%
  select(
    participant,
    condition,
    matches("^ext_resources_use_[1-6]$")
  ) %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols = matches("^ext_resources_use_[1-6]$"),
    names_to = "problem",
    names_pattern = "ext_resources_use_(\\d+)",
    values_to = "ext_resources",
    values_drop_na = TRUE
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    problem = factor(
      paste("Problem", problem),
      levels = paste("Problem", 1:6)
    ),
    ext_resources = case_when(
      ext_resources == "Yes" ~ 1,
      ext_resources == "No"  ~ 0,
      TRUE ~ NA_real_
    )
  ) %>%
  group_by(problem, condition) %>%
  summarise(
    percent = 100 * mean(ext_resources, na.rm = TRUE),
    N = sum(ext_resources, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    result = sprintf("%.2f%% (N = %d)", percent, N)
  ) %>%
  select(problem, condition, result) %>%
  pivot_wider(
    names_from = condition,
    values_from = result
  ) %>%
  knitr::kable(
    booktabs = TRUE,
    align = c("l", "c", "c", "c", "c"),
    caption = paste(
      "Percentage and number of responses reporting use of external",
      "resources, split by problem and condition."
    )
  ) #%>%

```

    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  mutate(

### Language background

```{r v2-chunk-011, echo=FALSE}
library(gt)

d_lang <- d %>%
  mutate(
    lang_fluency_clean = case_when(
      str_detect(lang_fluency, "^Beginner") ~ "Beginner",
      str_detect(lang_fluency, "^Intermediate") ~ "Intermediate",
      str_detect(lang_fluency, "^Advanced") ~ "Advanced",
      str_detect(lang_fluency, "^Expert/Proficient") ~ "Expert/Proficient",
      lang_fluency == "Prefer not to respond" ~ "Prefer not to respond",
      TRUE ~ NA_character_
    )
  )

native_summary <- d_lang %>%
  filter(!is.na(native_lang)) %>%
  count(response = native_lang) %>%
  mutate(
    section = "Native speaker of the study language",
    denominator = sum(n),
    percent = 100 * n / denominator
  )

fluency_summary <- d_lang %>%
  filter(
    native_lang == "No",
    !is.na(lang_fluency_clean)
  ) %>%
  count(response = lang_fluency_clean) %>%
  mutate(
    section = "Fluency among non-native speakers",
    denominator = sum(n),
    percent = 100 * n / denominator
  )

language_table <- bind_rows(
  native_summary,
  fluency_summary
) %>%
  mutate(
    response = factor(
      response,
      levels = c(
        "Yes", "No", "Prefer not to respond",
        "Beginner", "Intermediate", "Advanced",
        "Expert/Proficient"
      )
    )
  ) %>%
  arrange(section, response) %>%
  select(section, response, n, percent)

language_table %>%
  gt(groupname_col = "section") %>%
  cols_label(
    response = "Response",
    n = "N",
    percent = "%"
  ) %>%
  fmt_number(
    columns = percent,
    decimals = 1
  ) %>%
  tab_header(
    title = "Language background of participants"
  ) %>%
  tab_source_note(
    source_note = paste(
      "Fluency was assessed only among participants who reported",
      "that the study language was not their native language."
    )
  )
```

```{r models_H1, include=FALSE}
mH1_all <- v2_fit(glmer(correct_phase2 ~ feedback * justification + 
   (feedback * justification||Country), 
   family = binomial("logit"), data = dat_H1, 
   control = glmerControl(optimizer = "bobyqa", 
      optCtrl = list(maxfun = 1e5))))

mH1_i <- v2_fit(glmer(correct_phase2 ~ feedback * justification + 
   (feedback * justification||Country), 
   family = binomial("logit"), 
   data = dat_H1[dat_H1$culture == "Individualistic", ], 
   control = glmerControl(optimizer = "bobyqa", 
     optCtrl = list(maxfun = 1e5))))

mH1_c <- v2_fit(glmer(correct_phase2 ~ feedback * justification + 
   (feedback * justification||Country), 
   family = binomial("logit"), 
   data = dat_H1[dat_H1$culture == "Collectivistic", ], 
   control = glmerControl(optimizer = "bobyqa", 
      optCtrl = list(maxfun = 1e5))))

alpha <- 0.05
 
 
b_H1a <- fixef(mH1_all)["(Intercept)"]
SE_H1a <- sqrt(diag(vcov(mH1_all))["(Intercept)"])
z_H1a <- b_H1a / SE_H1a
p_value_H1a <- pnorm(z_H1a) # left-tailed test
H1a <- ifelse(p_value_H1a < alpha, 1, 0)
 
models <- list(mH1_i, mH1_c)
names <- c("Individualistic", "Collectivistic")
H1b_pvals <- numeric(length(models))
H1b_results <- numeric(length(models))
 
for (i in 1:length(models)) {
  b <- fixef(models[[i]])["(Intercept)"]
  SE <- sqrt(diag(vcov(models[[i]]))["(Intercept)"])
  z <- b / SE
  p_value <- pnorm(z) # left-tailed test
  H1b_pvals[i] <- p_value
  H1b_results[i] <- ifelse(p_value < alpha, 1, 0)
}

names(H1b_pvals) <- names
names(H1b_results) <- names

H1b <- ifelse(all(H1b_results == 1), 1, 0)

model_table <- function(model, caption = NULL, group = "Country",
                        term_labels = NULL, digits = 3) {

  tab_fixed <- broom.mixed::tidy(
    model,
    effects = "fixed",
    conf.int = TRUE
  )

  if (!is.null(term_labels)) {
    ii <- match(tab_fixed$term, names(term_labels))
    tab_fixed$term[!is.na(ii)] <- term_labels[ii[!is.na(ii)]]
  }

  tab_fixed <- tab_fixed %>%
    transmute(
      Predictor = term,
      Estimate = sprintf(paste0("%.", digits, "f"), estimate),
      SE = sprintf(paste0("%.", digits, "f"), std.error),
      `95% CI` = sprintf(
        paste0("[%.", digits, "f, %.", digits, "f]"),
        conf.low, conf.high
      ),
      `p-value` = case_when(
        p.value < .001 ~ "< .001",
        TRUE ~ sub("^0", "", sprintf("%.3f", p.value))
      )
    )

  vc <- as.data.frame(lme4::VarCorr(model)) %>%
    filter(is.na(var2))  # retain SDs, not correlations

  vc$grp <- sub("\\.[0-9]+$", "", vc$grp)

  if (!is.null(term_labels)) {
    ii <- match(vc$var1, names(term_labels))
    vc$var1[!is.na(ii)] <- term_labels[ii[!is.na(ii)]]
  }

  tab_random <- vc %>%
    filter(grp != "Residual") %>%
    transmute(
      Predictor = paste0("SD (", grp, ": ", var1, ")"),
      Estimate = sprintf(paste0("%.", digits, "f"), sdcor),
      SE = "",
      `95% CI` = "",
      `p-value` = ""
    )

  n <- nobs(model)

  n_groups <- if (group %in% names(model.frame(model))) {
    dplyr::n_distinct(model.frame(model)[[group]])
  } else {
    NA_integer_
  }

  tab_info <- tibble(
    Predictor = c("N", paste0("N ", group)),
    Estimate = c(as.character(n), as.character(n_groups)),
    SE = "",
    `95% CI` = "",
    `p-value` = ""
  )

  bind_rows(
    tab_fixed,
    tab_random,
    tab_info
  ) %>%
    knitr::kable(
      caption = caption,
      align = c("l", "r", "r", "c", "r")
    )
}

```{r v2-chunk-021, echo=FALSE}
format_p <- function(p, digits = 3) {
  case_when(
    is.na(p)  ~ NA_character_,
    p < 0.001 ~ "< .001",
    TRUE      ~ sub("^0", "", sprintf(paste0("%.", digits, "f"), p))
  )
}

format_culture_p <- function(p) {
  paste0(
    names(p),
    " = ",
    format_p(unname(p)),
    collapse = "; "
  )
}

H1a_supported <- H1a == 1
H1b_supported <- all(H1b_results == 1)

H2a_supported <- H2a == 1
H2b_supported <- all(H2b_results == 1)

H3a_supported <- H3a == 1
H3b_supported <- all(H3b_results == 1)

hypothesis_results <- tribble(
  ~Hypothesis, ~Prediction, ~Supported, ~`p-value(s)`,

  "H1a",
  "Less than half of correct answers will arise from error correction during deliberation",
  H1a_supported,
  format_p(p_value_H1a),

  "H1b",
  "Baseline performance is below 50% in both cultural groups",
  H1b_supported,
  format_culture_p(H1b_pvals),

  "H2a",
  "Feedback increases correction overall",
  H2a_supported,
  format_p(p_value_H2a),

  "H2b",
  "Feedback increases correction in both cultural groups",
  H2b_supported,
  format_culture_p(H2b_pvals),

  "H3a",
  "Justification increases correction overall",
  H3a_supported,
  format_p(p_value_H3a),

  "H3b",
  "Justification increases correction in both cultural groups",
  H3b_supported,
  format_culture_p(H3b_pvals)
) %>%
  mutate(
    Supported = case_when(
      is.na(Supported) ~ "Not estimable",
      Supported        ~ "Yes",
      TRUE             ~ "No"
    )
  )

hypothesis_results %>%
  kable(
    booktabs = TRUE,
    align = c("l", "l", "c", "l"),
    caption = paste(
      "Summary of preregistered hypothesis tests after including",
      "by-problem random intercepts"
    )
  ) # %>%

alpha <- 0.05
 
 
b_H1a <- fixef(mH1_all)["(Intercept)"]
SE_H1a <- sqrt(diag(vcov(mH1_all))["(Intercept)"])
z_H1a <- b_H1a / SE_H1a
p_value_H1a <- pnorm(z_H1a) # left-tailed test
H1a <- ifelse(p_value_H1a < alpha, 1, 0)
 
models <- list(mH1_i, mH1_c)
names <- c("Individualistic", "Collectivistic")
H1b_pvals <- numeric(length(models))
H1b_results <- numeric(length(models))
 
for (i in 1:length(models)) {
  b <- fixef(models[[i]])["(Intercept)"]
  SE <- sqrt(diag(vcov(models[[i]]))["(Intercept)"])
  z <- b / SE
  p_value <- pnorm(z) # left-tailed test
  H1b_pvals[i] <- p_value
  H1b_results[i] <- ifelse(p_value < alpha, 1, 0)
}

names(H1b_pvals) <- names
names(H1b_results) <- names

H1b <- ifelse(all(H1b_results == 1), 1, 0)

model_table_2 <- function(model, caption = NULL,
                        term_labels = NULL, digits = 3) {

  tab_fixed <- broom.mixed::tidy(
    model,
    effects = "fixed",
    conf.int = TRUE
  )

  if (!is.null(term_labels)) {
    ii <- match(tab_fixed$term, names(term_labels))
    tab_fixed$term[!is.na(ii)] <- term_labels[ii[!is.na(ii)]]
  }

  tab_fixed <- tab_fixed %>%
    transmute(
      Predictor = term,
      Estimate = sprintf(paste0("%.", digits, "f"), estimate),
      SE = sprintf(paste0("%.", digits, "f"), std.error),
      `95% CI` = sprintf(
        paste0("[%.", digits, "f, %.", digits, "f]"),
        conf.low, conf.high
      ),
      `p-value` = case_when(
        p.value < .001 ~ "< .001",
        TRUE ~ sub("^0", "", sprintf("%.3f", p.value))
      )
    )

  vc <- as.data.frame(lme4::VarCorr(model)) %>%
    filter(is.na(var2))  # variance/SD terms only

  vc$grp <- sub("\\.[0-9]+$", "", vc$grp)

  if (!is.null(term_labels)) {
    ii <- match(vc$var1, names(term_labels))
    vc$var1[!is.na(ii)] <- term_labels[ii[!is.na(ii)]]
  }

  tab_random <- vc %>%
    filter(grp != "Residual") %>%
    transmute(
      Predictor = paste0("SD (", grp, ": ", var1, ")"),
      Estimate = sprintf(paste0("%.", digits, "f"), sdcor),
      SE = "",
      `95% CI` = "",
      `p-value` = ""
    )

  n <- nobs(model)

  ng <- lme4::ngrps(model)

  tab_info <- tibble(
    Predictor = c(
      "N",
      paste0("N ", names(ng))
    ),
    Estimate = c(
      as.character(n),
      as.character(ng)
    ),
    SE = "",
    `95% CI` = "",
    `p-value` = ""
  )

  bind_rows(
    tab_fixed,
    tab_random,
    tab_info
  ) %>%
    knitr::kable(
      caption = caption,
      align = c("l", "r", "r", "c", "r")
    )
}

## Exploratory Analyses

### Continuous global collectivism (exploratory)

These models use the country-level Global Collectivism Index (GCI; named `CGI` in the dataset) on its original continuous scale, replacing the binary cultural grouping. Each model includes the full feedback × justification × GCI interaction and a problem random intercept. The H1 model uses the country random-effects structure in `scrap_continuous_models.R`; the correction model retains country random slopes for both manipulations and their interaction. These are exploratory associations with a country-level measure, not individual-level cultural effects. GCI = 0 is the reference for manipulation coefficients; the three-way term tests whether the feedback-by-justification interaction changes with GCI.

```{r continuous-gci-data}
gci_H1 <- dat_H1 %>% filter(is.finite(CGI), !is.na(correct_phase2))
gci_correction <- dat_Hother %>% filter(is.finite(CGI), !is.na(corrected))
gci_samples <- bind_rows(
  summarise(gci_H1, Outcome = "H1", Trials = n(), Participants = n_distinct(participant),
            Countries = n_distinct(Country), Minimum = min(CGI), Maximum = max(CGI)),
  summarise(gci_correction, Outcome = "Correction", Trials = n(), Participants = n_distinct(participant),
            Countries = n_distinct(Country), Minimum = min(CGI), Maximum = max(CGI)))
knitr::kable(gci_samples, digits = 2, caption = "Complete-case samples and observed GCI ranges.")
```

```{r continuous-gci-models}
mH1_all_cgi <- v2_fit(glmer(correct_phase2 ~ feedback * justification * CGI +
  (feedback + feedback:justification || Country) + (1 | problem),
  family = binomial("logit"), data = gci_H1,
  control = glmerControl(optimizer = "bobyqa", optCtrl = list(maxfun = 1e5))))
m_all_cgi <- v2_fit(glmer(corrected ~ feedback * justification * CGI +
  (feedback * justification || Country) + (1 | problem),
  family = binomial("logit"), data = gci_correction,
  control = glmerControl(optimizer = "bobyqa", optCtrl = list(maxfun = 1e5))))
model_table_2(mH1_all_cgi, caption = "Continuous GCI: correction during deliberation (H1 outcome).")
model_table_2(m_all_cgi, caption = "Continuous GCI: correction of initially incorrect responses.")
```

```{r continuous-gci-diagnostics}
v2_glmer_diagnostics <- function(model, label) {
  msg <- model@optinfo$conv$lme4$messages
  tibble(Model = label, Trials = nobs(model), Singular = isSingular(model),
         Optimizer_code = paste(model@optinfo$conv$opt, collapse = "; "),
         Convergence = if (is.null(msg)) "No lme4 convergence messages" else paste(msg, collapse = "; "))
}
knitr::kable(bind_rows(v2_glmer_diagnostics(mH1_all_cgi, "H1"),
                      v2_glmer_diagnostics(m_all_cgi, "Correction")),
             caption = "Continuous-GCI model diagnostics; inspect warnings before interpretation.")
```

```{r continuous-gci-predictions}
v2_gci_predictions <- function(model, data, label) {
  nd <- expand_grid(CGI = seq(min(data$CGI), max(data$CGI), length.out = 100),
                    feedback = 0:1, justification = 0:1)
  X <- model.matrix(~ feedback * justification * CGI, nd)
  X <- X[, names(fixef(model)), drop = FALSE]
  eta <- as.numeric(X %*% fixef(model))
  se <- sqrt(pmax(0, rowSums((X %*% as.matrix(vcov(model))) * X)))
  nd %>% mutate(fit = plogis(eta), lower = plogis(eta - 1.96 * se),
                upper = plogis(eta + 1.96 * se), Outcome = label,
                Feedback = factor(feedback, 0:1, c("No feedback", "Feedback")),
                Justification = factor(justification, 0:1, c("No justification", "Justification")))
}
pred_gci <- bind_rows(v2_gci_predictions(mH1_all_cgi, gci_H1, "H1 outcome"),
                      v2_gci_predictions(m_all_cgi, gci_correction, "Correction"))
saveRDS(pred_gci, file.path(v2_dir, "derived", "continuous-gci-predictions.rds"))
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-continuous-gci
#| fig-width: 8
#| fig-height: 5
#| fig-cap: "Predicted probabilities across the observed GCI range, by experimental condition. Bands are pointwise 95% Wald confidence intervals for fixed-effect predictions with random effects set to zero; they do not average over the random-effects distribution."
ggplot(pred_gci, aes(CGI, fit, colour = Feedback, fill = Feedback)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = lower, ymax = upper), alpha = .15, colour = NA) +
  geom_line() + facet_grid(Outcome ~ Justification) +
  labs(x = "Global Collectivism Index", y = "Predicted probability") + ml_theme()
```

### Scales reliability and measurement invariance

The IH and AOT analyses include countries with at least 100 observations; the IC measurement-invariance analysis uses at least 200 observations.

#### Intellectual humility

```{r v2-chunk-041}

IH_alpha_country <- d %>%
  group_by(Country) %>%
  group_modify(~{
    
    x <- .x[, IH_items]
    
    a <- tryCatch(
      psych::alpha(x, check.keys = FALSE, warnings = FALSE)$total$raw_alpha,
      error = function(e) NA_real_
    )
    
    tibble(
      N = nrow(.x),
      alpha = a
    )
    
  }) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  arrange(desc(N))

knitr::kable(
  IH_alpha_country[IH_alpha_country$N >= 100,],
  digits = 2,
  caption = "Internal consistency of the Intellectual Humility scale by country (only countries with N>100 shown)."
)
```

```{r v2-chunk-042, echo=FALSE, eval=FALSE}


IH_model <- '
  IH =~ IH_1 + IH_2 + IH_3 + IH_4 + IH_5 +
        IH_6 + IH_7 + IH_8 + IH_9

  POS =~ IH_1 + IH_2 + IH_3 + IH_4 + IH_5 + IH_7
  NEG =~ IH_6 + IH_8 + IH_9

  IH ~~ 0*POS
  IH ~~ 0*NEG

  POS ~~ NEG'

country_N <- table(d$Country)
countries_MI <- names(country_N[country_N >= 100])
d_IH_MI <- d %>%
  filter(Country %in% countries_MI)

fit_IH_config <- cfa(
  IH_model,
  data = d_IH_MI,
  group = "Country",
  estimator = "MLR",
  std.lv = TRUE,
  missing = "listwise"
)

POS_items <- c("IH_1", "IH_2", "IH_3", "IH_4", "IH_5", "IH_7")
NEG_items <- c("IH_6", "IH_8", "IH_9")

method_loadings <- c(
  paste0("POS=~", POS_items),
  paste0("NEG=~", NEG_items))

fit_IH_metric <- cfa(
  IH_model,
  data = d_IH_MI,
  group = "Country",
  estimator = "MLR",
  std.lv = TRUE,
  missing = "listwise",
  group.equal = "loadings",
  group.partial = method_loadings # Do NOT constrain wording-factor loadings (see note above)
)

fit_IH_scalar <- cfa(
  IH_model,
  data = d_IH_MI,
  group = "Country",
  estimator = "MLR",
  std.lv = TRUE,
  missing =  "listwise",
  group.equal = c("loadings", "intercepts"),
  group.partial = method_loadings
)

get_MI_fit <- function(fit) {
  fitMeasures(
    fit,
    c("cfi.robust", "tli.robust", "rmsea.robust", "srmr")
  )
}

fits_IH <- rbind(
  Configural = get_MI_fit(fit_IH_config),
  Metric     = get_MI_fit(fit_IH_metric),
  Scalar     = get_MI_fit(fit_IH_scalar)
)

fits_IH <- cbind(
  fits_IH,
  delta_CFI = c(
    NA,
    fits_IH["Metric", "cfi.robust"] -
      fits_IH["Configural", "cfi.robust"],
    fits_IH["Scalar", "cfi.robust"] -
      fits_IH["Metric", "cfi.robust"]
  ),
  delta_RMSEA = c(
    NA,
    fits_IH["Metric", "rmsea.robust"] -
      fits_IH["Configural", "rmsea.robust"],
    fits_IH["Scalar", "rmsea.robust"] -
      fits_IH["Metric", "rmsea.robust"]
  )
)

saveRDS(
  list(
    fits_IH = fits_IH,
    fit_IH_config = fit_IH_config,
    fit_IH_metric = fit_IH_metric,
    fit_IH_scalar = fit_IH_scalar
  ),
  file = file.path(v2_dir, "derived", "IH_measurement_invariance.rds")
)

```


```{r v2-chunk-043}
IH_MI <- readRDS("IH_measurement_invariance.rds")

fits_IH <- IH_MI$fits_IH

IH_fit_table <- as.data.frame(fits_IH) %>%
  tibble::rownames_to_column("Model") %>%
  transmute(
    Model,
    CFI = cfi.robust,
    TLI = tli.robust,
    RMSEA = rmsea.robust,
    SRMR = srmr,
    `ΔCFI` = delta_CFI,
    `ΔRMSEA` = delta_RMSEA
  )

knitr::kable(
  IH_fit_table,
  digits = 3,
  caption = "Measurement invariance analysis for the Intellectual Humility scale",
  align = c("l", rep("c", 6))
)
```

As an exploratory test of cross-country measurement invariance, we fitted multi-group CFAs in which the nine items loaded on a substantive intellectual-humility (IH) factor while separate positive- and negative-wording method factors captured the method effects identified in the original scale validation. The IH factor was specified as independent of the wording factors, while the two method factors were allowed to covary. The configural model showed good fit (CFI = .973, RMSEA = .050, SRMR = .029). We then constrained only the substantive IH loadings to equality across countries, leaving wording-factor loadings free; this produced a modest deterioration in fit (ΔCFI = −.017, ΔRMSEA = .005, ΔSRMR = .017). Adding equality constraints on item intercepts produced a larger deterioration (ΔCFI = −.032, ΔRMSEA = .009, ΔSRMR = .016). Thus, using the conventional ΔCFI ≤ .01 criterion, strict metric and scalar invariance were not supported, although departures from metric invariance were relatively modest. These results suggest that the scale captures a broadly similar construct across countries, but some caution is warranted.

#### Actively open-minded thinking scale


The table below uses the 13 AOT items after the reverse scoring already applied during data preparation. Raw Cronbach’s alpha is calculated using pairwise-complete item data, matching the IH reliability analysis; no automatic item reversal is applied. Countries with at least 100 participants are shown. Complete-item counts indicate how many participants answered every AOT item.

```{r aot-alpha-by-country}
AOT_alpha_country <- d %>%
  group_by(Country) %>%
  group_modify(~ {
    items <- .x[, AOT_items]
    alpha <- tryCatch(
      psych::alpha(items, check.keys = FALSE, warnings = FALSE,
                   use = "pairwise")$total$raw_alpha,
      error = function(e) NA_real_
    )
    tibble(N = nrow(.x), N_complete = sum(complete.cases(items)), alpha = alpha)
  }) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  arrange(desc(N), Country)

saveRDS(AOT_alpha_country, file.path(v2_dir, "derived", "aot-alpha-by-country.rds"))
knitr::kable(
  filter(AOT_alpha_country, N >= 100), digits = 2,
  col.names = c("Country", "N", "Complete-item N", "Cronbach's alpha"),
  caption = "Internal consistency of the Actively Open-Minded Thinking scale by country (N ≥ 100)."
)
```

The AOT scale showed mixed evidence of configural fit (CFI = .923, RMSEA = .051, SRMR = .044). When equality constraints were imposed only on the substantive AOT loadings, while allowing loadings on the negative-wording method factor to vary across countries, model fit deteriorated moderately (ΔCFI = −.034, ΔRMSEA = .005, ΔSRMR = .023), indicating departures from full metric invariance. Imposing equality constraints on item intercepts produced a much larger deterioration in fit (ΔCFI = −.139, ΔRMSEA = .022, ΔSRMR = .024), providing clear evidence against scalar invariance.


#### Individualistic and collectivistic cultural tendencies scale

> The original 1998 paper only reported that an EFA-supported four-factor structure, followed by convergent/discriminant validity analyses; they did not do an extensive four-factor CFA structure validation of the 16-items scale. 

> NOTE: post-fitting diagnostic check (`lavInspect(fit, "post.check")`) was failing for these model, in particular Egypt, Kuwait and Ghana (with N ranging from 110 to 183) had negative eigenvalues, indicating non-positive defined covariance matrices. Therefore I have increased the threshold for being included in the analysis from 100 to 200 responses (considering also that this is a more complex 4 factor model).

For the Individualism–Collectivism scale, measurement invariance was examined using the proposed four-factor structure (horizontal individualism, vertical individualism, horizontal collectivism, and vertical collectivism). Because models including smaller country samples produced inadmissible solutions, analyses were restricted to countries with at least 200 participants. The configural model showed mixed absolute fit (CFI = .833, RMSEA = .075, SRMR = .074), providing only moderate support for the four-factor structure across countries. Constraining factor loadings to equality resulted in a relatively small deterioration in fit (ΔCFI = −.018, ΔRMSEA = .000, ΔSRMR = .007); thus, strict metric invariance was not supported according to the conventional ΔCFI ≤ .01 criterion, although the results were broadly consistent with approximate metric comparability. In contrast, imposing equality constraints on item intercepts produced a substantial deterioration in fit (ΔCFI = −.191, ΔRMSEA = .027, ΔSRMR = .023), providing clear evidence against scalar invariance. Accordingly, associations involving the four dimensions may be reasonably comparable across countries, but cross-country comparisons of their observed mean levels should be interpreted with considerable caution.

### Individual differences and corrective behaviour (within-country centring)

In this version all scales are centred within country, to mitigate issues of violation of scalar invariance and improve comparability across countries.

<!-- ; and I have temporarily removed AOT as it showed more evidence for violation of metric invariance -->

```{r v2-chunk-053}

ID_vars <- c(
  "IH_score", "AOT_score",
  "IC_HI", "IC_VI", "IC_HC", "IC_VC"
)

dat_H1 <- dat_H1 %>%
  group_by(Country) %>%
  mutate(
    across(
      all_of(ID_vars),
      ~ .x - mean(.x, na.rm = TRUE),
      .names = "{.col}_wc"
    )
  ) %>%
  ungroup()

dat_Hother <- dat_Hother %>%
  group_by(Country) %>%
  mutate(
    across(
      all_of(ID_vars),
      ~ .x - mean(.x, na.rm = TRUE),
      .names = "{.col}_wc"
    )
  ) %>%
  ungroup()

```

### Community and Student Sample Differences

```{r v2-chunk-057, echo=FALSE}
table(d$Sample)
sum(is.na(d$Sample))

  filter(!is.na(Sample)) %>%
  group_by(culture, Sample) %>%

  filter(is.na(Sample)) %>%
  group_by(Country, LabID) %>%
  summarise(N = n())

d <- d %>%
  mutate(
    Sample = ifelse(
      Sample %in% c("Student", "Community"),
      Sample,
      NA_character_
    )
  )

d <- d %>%
  group_by(Country, LabID) %>%
  mutate(
    n_sample_types = n_distinct(Sample[!is.na(Sample)]),

    sample_inferred = ifelse(
      n_sample_types == 1,
      first(na.omit(Sample)),
      NA_character_
    ),

    Sample = coalesce(Sample, sample_inferred)
  ) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  select(-n_sample_types, -sample_inferred)

make_predictions <- function(model, accuracy_var, phase) {

  newdat <- expand_grid(
    accuracy = seq(0, 6, length.out = 121),
    IH_z = c(-1, 0, 1)
  )

  names(newdat)[names(newdat) == "accuracy"] <- accuracy_var

  pr <- predict(
    model,
    newdata = newdat,
    type = "response",
    se.fit = TRUE
  )

  newdat %>%
    mutate(
      fit = as.numeric(pr$fit),
      se = as.numeric(pr$se.fit),
      lower = fit - 1.96 * se,
      upper = fit + 1.96 * se,

      IH = factor(
        IH_z,
        levels = c(-1, 0, 1),
        labels = c(
          "IH: -1 SD",
          "IH: mean",
          "IH: +1 SD"
        )
      ),

      Phase = phase,

      accuracy = .data[[accuracy_var]]
    ) %>%
    select(
      accuracy, IH_z, IH,
      fit, lower, upper, Phase
    )
}

pred_int <- make_predictions(

```{r v2-chunk-063, echo=FALSE}
format_p <- function(p, digits = 3) {
  case_when(
    is.na(p)  ~ "",
    p < 0.001 ~ "< .001",
    TRUE      ~ sub("^0", "", sprintf(paste0("%.", digits, "f"), p))
  )
}

gam_model_table <- function(models,
                            caption = NULL,
                            model_labels = NULL,
                            term_labels = NULL,
                            digits = 3) {

  if (inherits(models, "gam")) {
    models <- list(Model = models)
  }

  if (is.null(names(models)) || any(names(models) == "")) {
    names(models) <- paste0("Model ", seq_along(models))
  }

  if (!is.null(model_labels)) {
    ii <- match(names(models), names(model_labels))
    names(models)[!is.na(ii)] <- model_labels[ii[!is.na(ii)]]
  }

  tab <- imap_dfr(models, function(model, model_name) {

    param <- broom::tidy(
      model,
      parametric = TRUE
    ) %>%
      transmute(
        Model = model_name,
        Component = "Parametric",
        Term = term,
        Estimate = sprintf(paste0("%.", digits, "f"), estimate),
        SE = sprintf(paste0("%.", digits, "f"), std.error),
        edf = "",
        `Ref. df` = "",
        Statistic = sprintf(paste0("%.", digits, "f"), statistic),
        p = format_p(p.value, digits)
      )

    smooth <- broom::tidy(
      model,
      parametric = FALSE
    ) %>%
      transmute(
        Model = model_name,
        Component = "Smooth",
        Term = term,
        Estimate = "",
        SE = "",
        edf = sprintf(paste0("%.", digits, "f"), edf),
        `Ref. df` = sprintf(paste0("%.", digits, "f"), ref.df),
        Statistic = sprintf(paste0("%.", digits, "f"), statistic),
        p = format_p(p.value, digits)
      )

    bind_rows(param, smooth)
  })

  if (!is.null(term_labels)) {
    ii <- match(tab$Term, names(term_labels))
    tab$Term[!is.na(ii)] <- term_labels[ii[!is.na(ii)]]
  }

  knitr::kable(
    tab,
    format = "pipe",
    align = c("l", "l", "l", "r", "r", "r", "r", "r", "r"),
    caption = caption
  )
}
```

#### Binned observations for the calibration plots

The additional plot versions overlay participant-level mean estimates of performance, with **±1 standard error** bars. Only participants with complete data for the relevant phase and IH contribute to a bin. Accuracy levels **1–6** are displayed, giving 12 median-split points or 30 quintile points per phase; zero-correct observations remain in the fitted models and original plots.

For the accuracy-axis plots, one median IH cutoff is calculated across participants in the calibration dataset and used for both phases and every accuracy level. Scores equal to the median belong to the lower group, so ties may make the group sizes unequal. Point shapes distinguish these two observed groups; the original three curves still show predictions at mean IH and ±1 SD, rather than predictions averaged over the median-split groups.

For the IH-axis plots, participants are sorted by IH within each phase and accuracy level and divided into five bins with counts differing by at most one. Ties in IH are ordered by participant ID and may span bins. Points are placed at each bin’s mean IH and mean estimated performance, and their colours match the corresponding accuracy curves. Error bars describe variability across participant estimates; they are distinct from the model confidence bands.

```{r calibration-observation-bins}
calib_IH_median <- median(tab_calib$IH_score[is.finite(tab_calib$IH_z)], na.rm = TRUE)
calib_observed <- bind_rows(
  tab_calib %>% transmute(participant, IH_score, IH_z,
    Phase = "Intuitive phase", accuracy = accuracy_intuitive, estimate = calib_int),
  tab_calib %>% transmute(participant, IH_score, IH_z,
    Phase = "Reflective phase", accuracy = accuracy_reflective, estimate = calib_ref)
) %>%
  filter(is.finite(estimate), is.finite(IH_score), is.finite(IH_z), accuracy %in% 1:6) %>%
  mutate(
    IH_group = factor(if_else(IH_score <= calib_IH_median,
      "At/below IH median", "Above IH median"),
      levels = c("At/below IH median", "Above IH median")),
    accuracy_level = factor(accuracy, levels = 1:6)
  )

calib_bins_median <- calib_observed %>%
  group_by(Phase, accuracy, IH_group) %>%
  summarise(n = n(), IH_mean = mean(IH_score), mean_estimate = mean(estimate),
            se = sd(estimate) / sqrt(n()), .groups = "drop")

calib_quintile_membership <- calib_observed %>%
  arrange(Phase, accuracy, IH_score, participant) %>%
  group_by(Phase, accuracy, accuracy_level) %>%
  mutate(IH_bin = ntile(row_number(), 5L)) %>%
  ungroup()
calib_bins_quintile <- calib_quintile_membership %>%
  group_by(Phase, accuracy, accuracy_level, IH_bin) %>%
  summarise(n = n(), IH_mean = mean(IH_score), mean_estimate = mean(estimate),
            se = sd(estimate) / sqrt(n()), .groups = "drop")

# Fail visibly if the requested layout cannot be supported by the data.
stopifnot(all(count(calib_bins_median, Phase)$n == 12L),
          all(count(calib_bins_quintile, Phase)$n == 30L),
          all(calib_bins_median$n >= 2L), all(calib_bins_quintile$n >= 2L))
saveRDS(list(median_cutoff = calib_IH_median, median = calib_bins_median,
             quintile = calib_bins_quintile),
        file.path(v2_dir, "derived", "calibration-observed-bins.rds"))

v2_plot_calibration_bins <- function(predictions) {
  dodge <- position_dodge(width = 0.16)
  ggplot(predictions, aes(accuracy, fit, colour = IH, fill = IH)) +
    geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = lower, ymax = upper), alpha = .15, colour = NA) +
    geom_line(linewidth = 1) +
    geom_abline(intercept = 0, slope = 1, linetype = 2) +
    geom_errorbar(data = calib_bins_median,
      aes(x = accuracy, ymin = mean_estimate - se, ymax = mean_estimate + se,
          group = IH_group), inherit.aes = FALSE, position = dodge,
      width = .10, colour = "black", linewidth = .4) +
    geom_point(data = calib_bins_median,
      aes(x = accuracy, y = mean_estimate, shape = IH_group),
      inherit.aes = FALSE, position = dodge, colour = "black", size = 2) +
    facet_wrap(~Phase, nrow = 1) +
    scale_colour_viridis_d() + scale_fill_viridis_d() +
    scale_shape_manual(values = c(16, 17)) +
    coord_equal(xlim = c(0, 6), ylim = c(0, 6)) +
    scale_x_continuous(breaks = 0:6) + scale_y_continuous(breaks = 0:6) +
    labs(x = "Actual accuracy", y = "Estimated number correct",
         colour = "Model IH", fill = "Model IH", shape = "Observed IH group") +
    ml_theme() + theme(legend.position = "bottom")
}

v2_plot_ih_bins <- function(predictions, ih_column) {
  ggplot(predictions, aes(x = .data[[ih_column]], y = fit,
                         colour = accuracy_level, fill = accuracy_level)) +
    geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = lower, ymax = upper), alpha = .12, colour = NA) +
    geom_line(linewidth = 1) +
    geom_errorbar(data = calib_bins_quintile,
      aes(x = IH_mean, ymin = mean_estimate - se, ymax = mean_estimate + se,
          colour = accuracy_level), inherit.aes = FALSE, width = .06, linewidth = .4) +
    geom_point(data = calib_bins_quintile,
      aes(x = IH_mean, y = mean_estimate, colour = accuracy_level),
      inherit.aes = FALSE, size = 2) +
    facet_wrap(~Phase, nrow = 1) +
    scale_colour_viridis_d(drop = FALSE) + scale_fill_viridis_d(drop = FALSE) +
    scale_y_continuous(breaks = 0:6) + coord_cartesian(xlim = c(1, 7)) +
    labs(x = "Intellectual humility", y = "Estimated number correct",
         colour = "Actual accuracy", fill = "Actual accuracy") + ml_theme()
}

```{r}
#| fig-align: 'center'

#| fig-width: 8
#| fig-height: 4
#| fig-cap: "Intellectual humility, actual accuracy, and estimated performance. Generalised additive models (GAMs) predicting participants’ estimated number of correct answers from actual accuracy and intellectual humility, fitted separately for the intuitive (left) and reflective (right) phases. Lines show model-predicted estimates across the observed range of intellectual humility scores, plotted separately for each level of actual accuracy; shaded bands indicate 95% confidence intervals. In the intuitive phase, intellectual humility was associated with a small overall downward shift in estimated performance across accuracy levels. In the reflective phase, the association between intellectual humility and estimated performance varied modestly as a function of actual accuracy, consistent with a small but significant interaction."
#| label: fig-calibration-model-2

 
make_IH_predictions <- function(model,
                                data,
                                accuracy_var,
                                phase,
                                accuracy_values = 1:6,
                                n_IH = 200) {
  
  
  IH_seq <- (seq(1,7,length.out = n_IH) - mean(tab_calib$IH_score, na.rm = TRUE))/sd(tab_calib$IH_score, na.rm = TRUE)
  
  newdat <- expand_grid(
    IH_z = IH_seq,
    accuracy = accuracy_values
  )
  
  names(newdat)[names(newdat) == "accuracy"] <- accuracy_var
  
  pr <- predict(
    model,
    newdata = newdat,
    type = "response",
    se.fit = TRUE
  )
  
  newdat %>%
    mutate(
      fit   = as.numeric(pr$fit),
      se    = as.numeric(pr$se.fit),
      lower = fit - 1.96 * se,
      upper = fit + 1.96 * se,
      accuracy_level = factor(.data[[accuracy_var]],
                              levels = accuracy_values),
      Phase = phase
    )
}

  model = m_calib_int,
  data = tab_calib,
  accuracy_var = "accuracy_intuitive",
  phase = "Intuitive phase",
  accuracy_values = 1:6
)

pred_IH_ref <- make_IH_predictions(
  model = m_calib_ref,
  data = tab_calib,
  accuracy_var = "accuracy_reflective",
  phase = "Reflective phase",
  accuracy_values = 1:6
)

#### Robustness analysis: quasibinomial GAMs

As a robustness analysis, we repeated the calibration analyses using quasibinomial GAMs. These models constrain predicted estimates to the possible 0–6 range while allowing for overdispersion relative to the binomial variance.

```{r}
#| label: gam-quasibinomial
#| warning: false
#| message: false

library(mgcv)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(patchwork)

m_calib_int_qbin <- v2_fit(gam(
  cbind(calib_int, 6 - calib_int) ~
    s(accuracy_intuitive, k = 7, bs = "cr") +
    s(IH_z, k = 5) +
    ti(
      accuracy_intuitive,
      IH_z,
      k = c(7, 5),
      bs = c("cr", "tp")
    ),
  family = quasibinomial(link = "logit"),
  data = tab_calib,
  method = "REML"
))

m_calib_ref_qbin <- v2_fit(gam(
  cbind(calib_ref, 6 - calib_ref) ~
    s(accuracy_reflective, k = 7, bs = "cr") +
    s(IH_z, k = 5) +
    ti(
      accuracy_reflective,
      IH_z,
      k = c(7, 5),
      bs = c("cr", "tp")
    ),
  family = quasibinomial(link = "logit"),
  data = tab_calib,
  method = "REML"
))

```

#### Predicted calibration curves

```{r}
#| label: fig-gam-qbin-calibration
#| fig-cap: "Quasibinomial robustness analysis of intellectual humility and calibration of estimated performance. Lines show model-predicted estimates at the mean and ±1 SD of intellectual humility; shaded bands indicate 95% confidence intervals. The dashed diagonal indicates perfect calibration."
#| fig-width: 8
#| fig-height: 4
#| fig-align: 'center'

make_qbin_calib_predictions <- function(model,
                                        accuracy_var,
                                        phase) {

  newdat <- expand_grid(
    accuracy = seq(0, 6, length.out = 121),
    IH_z = c(-1, 0, 1)
  )

  names(newdat)[names(newdat) == "accuracy"] <- accuracy_var

  pr <- predict(
    model,
    newdata = newdat,
    type = "link",
    se.fit = TRUE
  )

  newdat %>%
    mutate(
      eta = as.numeric(pr$fit),
      se = as.numeric(pr$se.fit),

      fit   = 6 * plogis(eta),
      lower = 6 * plogis(eta - 1.96 * se),
      upper = 6 * plogis(eta + 1.96 * se),

      IH = factor(
        IH_z,
        levels = c(-1, 0, 1),
        labels = c(
          "IH: -1 SD",
          "IH: mean",
          "IH: +1 SD"
        )
      ),

      Phase = phase,
      accuracy = .data[[accuracy_var]]
    ) %>%
    select(
      accuracy, IH_z, IH,
      fit, lower, upper, Phase
    )
}

pred_qbin_int <- make_qbin_calib_predictions(
  m_calib_int_qbin,
  "accuracy_intuitive",

)

pred_qbin_ref <- make_qbin_calib_predictions(

Lines show model-predicted estimates across the observed range of intellectual humility scores, separately for each level of actual accuracy; shaded bands indicate 95% confidence intervals."

IH_sd   <- sd(tab_calib$IH_score, na.rm = TRUE)

make_qbin_IH_predictions <- function(model,
                                     data,
                                     accuracy_var,
                                     phase,
                                     accuracy_values = 1:6,
                                     n_IH = 200) {

  IH_raw <- seq(
    min(data$IH_score, na.rm = TRUE),
    max(data$IH_score, na.rm = TRUE),
    length.out = n_IH
  )

  newdat <- expand_grid(
    IH_score = IH_raw,
    accuracy = accuracy_values
  ) %>%
    mutate(
      IH_z = (IH_score - IH_mean) / IH_sd
    )

  names(newdat)[names(newdat) == "accuracy"] <- accuracy_var

  pr <- predict(
    model,
    newdata = newdat,
    type = "link",
    se.fit = TRUE
  )

  newdat %>%
    mutate(
      eta = as.numeric(pr$fit),
      se = as.numeric(pr$se.fit),

      fit   = 6 * plogis(eta),
      lower = 6 * plogis(eta - 1.96 * se),
      upper = 6 * plogis(eta + 1.96 * se),

      accuracy_level = factor(
        .data[[accuracy_var]],
        levels = accuracy_values
      ),

      Phase = phase
    )
}

### Confidence Resolution and Intellectual Humility

Confidence resolution is the difference in confidence between correct and incorrect answers. Separate Gaussian GAMMs are fitted for the intuitive and reflective phases, with correctness-specific smooths of intellectual humility (IH), fixed problem effects, and participant random intercepts. Trials reporting external-resource use and trials with missing confidence, accuracy, or IH are excluded. IH is standardised once across participants before trial filtering. Curves below average equally over problems; the resolution contrast uses the full coefficient covariance matrix. Intervals are pointwise, not simultaneous, and Gaussian predictions are not constrained to the confidence scale.

```{r v2-chunk-071}

library(gamm4)

IH_scaling <- d_long %>% distinct(participant, IH_score)
IH_center <- mean(IH_scaling$IH_score, na.rm = TRUE)
IH_scale <- sd(IH_scaling$IH_score, na.rm = TRUE)
IH_par <- IH_scaling %>%
  mutate(
    IH_z = as.numeric(scale(IH_score))
  ) %>%
  select(participant, IH_z)

dat_conf <- d_long %>%
  left_join(IH_par, by = "participant") %>%
  filter(
    ext_resources_use == "No",
    !is.na(confidence),
    !is.na(accuracy),
    !is.na(IH_z)
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    correctness = factor(
      accuracy,
      levels = c(0, 1),
      labels = c("Incorrect", "Correct")
    ),
    participant = factor(participant),
    problem = factor(problem)
)

contrasts(dat_conf$problem) <- contr.sum(nlevels(dat_conf$problem))
```

```{r confidence-resolution-predictions}
make_conf_predictions <- function(model, data, phase, n = 200) {
  
  IH_seq <- seq(
    min(data$IH_z, na.rm = TRUE),
    max(data$IH_z, na.rm = TRUE),
    length.out = n
  )
  
  newdat <- expand_grid(
    IH_z = IH_seq,
    correctness = factor(
      c("Incorrect", "Correct"),
      levels = c("Incorrect", "Correct")
    ),
    problem = levels(data$problem)
  ) %>%
    mutate(
      problem = factor(
        problem,
        levels = levels(data$problem)
      )
    )
  
  contrasts(newdat$problem) <- contr.sum(nlevels(data$problem))
  
  Xp <- predict(
    model$gam,
    newdata = newdat,
    type = "lpmatrix"
  )
  
  newdat$pred_id <- interaction(
    newdat$IH_z,
    newdat$correctness,
    drop = TRUE
  )
  
  ids <- unique(newdat$pred_id)
  
  Xbar <- do.call(
    rbind,
    lapply(ids, function(id) {
      colMeans(Xp[newdat$pred_id == id, , drop = FALSE])
    })
  )
  
  pred_dat <- newdat %>%
    distinct(pred_id, IH_z, correctness) %>%
    arrange(match(pred_id, ids))
  
  beta <- coef(model$gam)
  V <- vcov(model$gam)
  
  pred_dat %>%
    mutate(
      fit = as.numeric(Xbar %*% beta),
      
      se = sqrt(
        rowSums((Xbar %*% V) * Xbar)
      ),
      
      lower = fit - 1.96 * se,
      upper = fit + 1.96 * se,
      
      Phase = phase
    )
}

pred_conf_int <- make_conf_predictions(
  m_conf_int,
  dat_int,
  "Intuitive phase"
)

pred_conf_ref <- make_conf_predictions(
  m_conf_ref,
  dat_ref,
  "Reflective phase"
)

pred_conf <- bind_rows(
  pred_conf_int,
  pred_conf_ref
)

IH_par <- dat_conf %>%
  distinct(participant, IH_score, IH_z)

IH_mean <- IH_center
IH_sd <- IH_scale

pred_conf <- pred_conf %>%
  mutate(
    IH_score = IH_z * IH_sd + IH_mean
  )

```

```{r}
#| label: fig-confidence-resolution
#| fig-width: 8
#| fig-height: 4
#| fig-cap: "Trial-level confidence by IH and correctness. Curves and pointwise 95% intervals average equally across problems. Points are problem-adjusted participant means grouped into 30 IH bins within phase and correctness; error bars are descriptive ±1 SE across participant means and exclude model-adjustment uncertainty. Dashed lines show mean participant accuracy, as a descriptive reference only."
adjust_for_problem <- function(model, data) {
  
  pred_actual <- predict(
    model$gam,
    newdata = data,
    type = "response"
  )
  
  problem_levels <- levels(data$problem)
  
  pred_average_problem <- sapply(
    problem_levels,
    function(p) {
      
      nd <- data
      nd$problem <- factor(
        p,
        levels = problem_levels
      )
      
      predict(
        model$gam,
        newdata = nd,
        type = "response"
      )
    }
  ) %>%
    rowMeans()
  
  problem_effect <- pred_actual - pred_average_problem
  
  data %>%
    mutate(
      confidence_adjusted =
        confidence - problem_effect
    )
}

dat_int_adj <- adjust_for_problem(
  m_conf_int,
  dat_int
)

dat_ref_adj <- adjust_for_problem(
  m_conf_ref,
  dat_ref
)

dat_conf_adj <- bind_rows(
  dat_int_adj %>%
    mutate(Phase = "Intuitive phase"),
  
  dat_ref_adj %>%
    mutate(Phase = "Reflective phase")
)

participant_conf_adj <- dat_conf_adj %>%
  group_by(
    participant,
    Phase,
    correctness
  ) %>%
  summarise(
    IH_score = first(IH_score),
    
    mean_confidence =
      mean(confidence_adjusted, na.rm = TRUE),
    
    .groups = "drop"
  )

binned_conf_adj <- participant_conf_adj %>%
  group_by(Phase, correctness) %>%
  mutate(
    IH_bin = ntile(IH_score, 30)
  ) %>%
  group_by(Phase, correctness, IH_bin) %>%
  summarise(
    IH_score = mean(IH_score, na.rm = TRUE),
    
    n_participants = n(),
    
    se_confidence =
      sd(mean_confidence, na.rm = TRUE) /
      sqrt(n_participants),
    
    mean_confidence =
      mean(mean_confidence, na.rm = TRUE),
    
    .groups = "drop"
  )

mean_accuracy <- dat_conf %>%
  group_by(condition, participant) %>%
  summarise(
    accuracy = mean(accuracy, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%

    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%

      "intuitive" = "Intuitive phase",
      "reflective" = "Reflective phase"
    )
  )

ggplot(

  aes(
    x = IH_score,

) +

#### Resolution contrasts

A positive contrast means higher confidence for correct than incorrect answers. Separate significant smooths do not themselves establish that resolution varies with IH; the contrast curve and its uncertainty address the difference directly. These exploratory pointwise intervals do not provide a multiplicity-adjusted global test of moderation.

```{r confidence-resolution-contrasts}
v2_resolution <- function(model, data, phase) {
  ranges <- data %>% group_by(correctness) %>% summarise(lo = min(IH_z), hi = max(IH_z), .groups = "drop")
  z <- seq(max(ranges$lo), min(ranges$hi), length.out = 100)
  average_X <- function(correct) {
    nd <- expand_grid(IH_z = z, problem = levels(data$problem)) %>%
      mutate(problem = factor(problem, levels = levels(data$problem)),
             correctness = factor(correct, levels = levels(data$correctness)))
    contrasts(nd$problem) <- contr.sum(nlevels(nd$problem))
    X <- predict(model$gam, nd, type = "lpmatrix")
    t(vapply(z, function(v) colMeans(X[nd$IH_z == v, , drop = FALSE]), numeric(ncol(X))))
  }
  D <- average_X("Correct") - average_X("Incorrect")
  fit <- as.numeric(D %*% coef(model$gam))
  se <- sqrt(pmax(0, rowSums((D %*% vcov(model$gam)) * D)))
  tibble(IH_score = z * IH_scale + IH_center, fit = fit,
         lower = fit - 1.96 * se, upper = fit + 1.96 * se, Phase = phase)
}
pred_resolution <- bind_rows(v2_resolution(m_conf_int, dat_int, "Intuitive phase"),
                             v2_resolution(m_conf_ref, dat_ref, "Reflective phase"))
saveRDS(list(curves = pred_conf, observed = binned_conf_adj, contrasts = pred_resolution),
        file.path(v2_dir, "derived", "confidence-resolution.rds"))
```

#| label: fig-resolution-contrast
#| fig-width: 8
#| fig-height: 4
#| fig-cap: "Confidence resolution (correct minus incorrect) over the overlapping observed IH range. Bands are pointwise 95% intervals incorporating covariance between both fitted curves."
ggplot(pred_resolution, aes(IH_score, fit)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = lower, ymax = upper), alpha = .15) + geom_line() +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = 2) + facet_wrap(~Phase) +
  labs(x = "Intellectual humility", y = "Confidence difference: correct − incorrect") + ml_theme()
```
